title: Tenant-aware embedding rollout and semantics regression hub
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Add a tenant-aware, low-risk onboarding path for new embedding models and a semantics regression hub that quantitatively detects distribution and quality regressions during rollouts. This work will reduce surprise regressions in production reranking/semantic search, keep p99 latency stable under mixed-model serving, and provide automated gates and rollback triggers. Scope includes: (1) new canary traffic scheduler that enforces per-tenant traffic caps and gradual ramps; (2) a semantics regression hub service that ingests batch evals and live-sampled similarity distributions; (3) compatibility matrix automation for tokenizers/embedding-dim/quant profiles; (4) migration helpers (model-aliasing, preview endpoints, client-side SDK hints); (5) dashboards and runbook updates for ops/SEs. Out of scope: wholesale retraining of models or changes to embedding distance metrics themselves.
acceptance_criteria: Can schedule a canary rollout that routes 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% of a tenant's traffic to the new embedding model with automated waits configured between steps

Semantics regression hub produces a daily report comparing baseline and candidate: similarity distribution shift (KS test), top-k rerank precision delta, and embedding cosine drift per-corpus, viewable in the console
Automated compatibility checks fail rollout if tokenizer mismatch or embedding-dim mismatch is detected for >0 tenants
Latency impact measured: 95th percentile latency across affected tenants does not regress by more than 10ms during 25% ramp; p99 preserved within 30ms with configured fallback policies
Rollback triggers implemented: semantic delta > threshold OR error-rate spike > 2x baseline OR sustained latency regression > alert threshold; rollback can be executed automatically or manually
Migration doc + SDK snippet and a preview endpoint are available, and at least two integration tests in the CI verify alias-based transparent switch for client code
plan: Design: finalize semantics regression metrics, threshold defaults, and per-tenant ramp policy (owner: Aaron)
Instrument: add sample-capture hook in rerank/embeddings endpoints that emits anonymized similarity pairs and latency histograms (owner: infra-team)
Hub: implement a lightweight service that runs nightly batch comparisons and stores KS test, mean cosine difference, top-k precision deltas (owner: analytics)
Scheduler: implement tenant-aware traffic caps and ramp controller with feature-flag gating (LaunchDarkly) and config in model-catalog (owner: serving)
Tests: add synthetic and real-corpus smoke tests, compatibility matrix checks, and canary e2e tests to CI (owner: qa)
Dashboard & Runbook: add visualization panels and incident playbook for rollback and mitigation (owner: observability)
Pilot: run with 5 internal tenants for 2 weeks, collect telemetry, iterate on thresholds, then open for opt-in external customers
notes: Design decision: use KS test + mean cosine delta + top-k precision as the primary regression signals. Chosen because KS captures distributional shifts even when mean drift is small.
Trade-off: higher sensitivity to small shifts increases false positives; mitigated via tiered thresholds and requiring two signals to trigger auto-rollback.
Performance note: we will sample at most 1% of requests for similarity capture, capped per-tenant to avoid extra load on hot tenants.
Implementation detail: model-alias mapping will live in model-catalog and support 'legacy' fallback alias. SDK will prefer alias resolution with transparent swap.
PRs: initial scheduler prototype at github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4127, semantics hub baseline at github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/288
